blockingProblems: THESIS CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN CONTENTS. Line 9 states the chapter's spine: 'The transitions in this chapter all fail at that first step, in ways that share nothing but the location of the failure.' The first step is identifying an order parameter. But line 49 says of percolation, 'Everything else the previous chapter's machinery describes is present. The order parameter is the probability P_infty(p)...' and line 73 says of quantum criticality, 'The order-parameter concept survives the move.' Two of the four cases explicitly do NOT fail at the first step. Percolation fails at the free energy; quantum criticality fails at the control parameter and the accessibility of the critical point. The organising claim is false of half the chapter, and the chapter itself says so without noticing. A Cambridge referee would send this back on this point alone.

THE BOOK'S SUBJECT IS ABSENT. The research packet's own outline states the chapter's purpose: 'Not every transition fits the Landau picture, and the exceptions are where machine learning has been most useful, because they are where human intuition about order parameters runs out.' Machine learning, AI, or learned representations appear nowhere in 4,631 words. The only gestures are line 107 ('the direct ancestors of the material in Part Six of this book') and a vague clause at line 115 about 'instruments that produce more data than any person can inspect.' As delivered this is a competent history-of-statistical-physics chapter that would sit unchanged in a book with no AI in it. Chapter 3 of a book on AI and phase transitions cannot decline to be about the book.

THE OPENING HOOK IS NEVER PAID OFF. The chapter opens on the negative zero-point entropy of the replica-symmetric Sherrington-Kirkpatrick solution and calls it the fault line of the whole chapter (lines 3-5). It never states the value, never shows where it comes from, and never shows how replica symmetry produces it. Line 91 simply asserts 'The negative entropy was the signal that this innocuous step was the wrong one.' The reader is promised a specific quantitative impossibility and given a slogan. Worse, line 5 says 'Establishing which part of that form was wrong took four years,' but the actual diagnosis was the de Almeida-Thouless instability analysis, which the chapter mentions only at line 101 in a completely different context (the droplet dispute) and never connects back to the opening. The chapter's own narrative arc has a hole in the middle of it.

NEAR-VERBATIM DEPENDENCE ON THE RESEARCH PACKET. Multiple passages are the packet's claim text with the seams sanded. Packet on Millis: 'determines when it is legitimate to integrate out the fermions and describe criticality by an effective bosonic theory retaining only order-parameter fluctuations, and by solving the appropriate scaling equations obtains the distinct regimes of the correlation length and free energy in the disordered phase — with results differing from Hertz's in several cases.' Chapter line 75: 'asking when the fermions may legitimately be integrated out and the criticality described by an effective bosonic theory of order-parameter fluctuations alone, and by solving the appropriate scaling equations obtained the distinct regimes of the correlation length and the free energy in the disordered phase, with results differing from Hertz's in several cases.' Same for Newman-Stein (line 103 versus packet), and for Kosterlitz 1974 (line 15 is the packet sentence verbatim). This matters substantively, not just stylistically: the packet flags its own Millis description as 'from APS abstract-page snippets, not from a verbatim read.' The chapter is therefore paraphrasing a paraphrase of an abstract snippet and presenting it to the reader as a characterisation of what Millis argued.

ONLY ONE OF FOUR CASES IS ACTUALLY DERIVED. The BKT free-energy balance (lines 17-33) is properly worked. Nothing else is. The Fortuin-Kasteleyn expansion at line 51-53 says 'expand each bond factor into a term with the bond present and a term with it absent. Summing over the labels leaves a sum over subsets B' and then prints the answer; the cluster factor q^{c(B)} and the identification p = 1 - e^{-beta J} are asserted, not obtained. The quantum-critical slab argument (line 61) is one sentence and never explains where z actually comes from in an itinerant magnet, which is the entire content of Hertz's construction. Parisi's scheme (line 93) is 'breaking the permutation symmetry among the replicas in a nested, hierarchical way' and nothing more; the nested block matrix and the limit that produces q(x) never appear. A graduate student finishes this chapter able to reproduce exactly one calculation.

NO NUMBERS ANYWHERE OUTSIDE THE BKT ALGEBRA. beta, nu and d_f are named for percolation at line 49 with no values in any dimension. The negative entropy has no value. The dynamical exponent gets a bare 'z = 2' at line 65 with no derivation and no statement of which magnet. K/k_B T = 2/pi at line 33 is the only quantitative result in the chapter. Published monographs on this material anchor the reader with numbers; this reads as a chapter written from bibliographic metadata rather than from the physics.
styleViolations: No automatic-FAIL style violations found, and I checked mechanically rather than by eye. Em dashes (U+2014): 0. En dashes (U+2013): 0. Literal '--': 0. Unicode minus: 0. The only non-ASCII characters in the file are the diacritics in Löhneysen, Wölfle and Pépin. No bullet, dash, asterisk or numbered-list lines anywhere. No end-of-chapter summary or recap section. The ending (line 115, 'The question is how anyone would ever know.') is genuinely open and does leave the reader curious.

Not an automatic violation but a real one: the chapter contains a numbered list wearing a coat. Line 9 announces the enumeration ('The transitions in this chapter all fail at that first step'), then line 47 opens 'A second kind of exception is older and simpler,' then line 59 opens 'The third exception moves the control knob.' That is items one through three of a list, rendered as topic sentences. The prohibition on lists exists to force the prose to carry its own connective logic; here the scaffolding is simply transcribed into sentences, and because the enumeration is false (see blocking problems) the scaffolding is load-bearing and wrong.

Full-legal-name mannerism throughout, and it is the clearest tell that this was generated from a metadata field rather than written. 'Lev Davidovich Landau' (7), 'Kenneth Geddes Wilson' (7), 'Norman David Mermin' (13), 'Vadim Lvovich Berezinskii' (15), 'John Michael Kosterlitz and David James Thouless' (15), 'Simon Ralph Broadbent and John Michael Hammersley' (47), 'Samuel Frederick Edwards and Philip Warren Anderson' (83), 'Philip Warren Anderson' (111). Every one of these matches the 'people' field of the corresponding packet entry. No monograph writes 'Norman David Mermin and Herbert Wagner proved'; it writes 'Mermin and Wagner proved.'
Internal inconsistency in the same mannerism: 'Kenneth Geddes Wilson' at line 7, 'Kenneth G. Wilson' at line 65. Same man, two forms, ten paragraphs apart.

Two different Fishers appear with no signal to the reader. 'Michael E. Fisher' at line 65 (epsilon expansion) and 'Daniel S. Fisher' at line 101 (droplet picture). In a chapter whose second half is a spin-glass controversy, letting an unqualified surname collision stand is an editorial failure.

Cross-section repetition of the chapter's own best idea, the second time presented as if new. Line 41: 'the object it asks for is of a type this system does not possess.' Line 99: 'The resulting order parameter is not a scalar, not a vector, and not a tensor, but a function.' Line 113: 'the new laws may require mathematical objects of a kind not present anywhere in the description of the level below' and 'Its solution is a function on the unit interval encoding an ultrametric tree of states.' Four statements of one thought.

'## Citations used in this chapter' (line 117) is a working-document heading, not a book heading. No university press prints that phrase. The apparatus also does not match the body: line 15 cites 'Journal of Physics C 7, 1046-1060 (1974)' and line 87 cites 'Journal of Physics F: Metal Physics 6, 1927 (1976)' inline with full volume and page, and neither appears in the list.
factProblems: Credit where due, since it is unusual: I found no fabricated person, paper, year, venue or institution. Every named entity traces to the packet's verifiedClaims, and all five substantive packet corrections were actually applied. Berezinskii's Russian original is dated 1970 with English translation 1971 (line 15, citation line 123), not the propagated 1971 error. The Sauer translation is EPJ Special Topics 226, 539-549 (2017), not the packet's original wrong year and volume (citation line 121). The 2021 Nobel citation includes 'physical' (line 107). The 2016 Nobel split is one half / one quarter / one quarter, correctly worded (line 43). Millis carries no affiliation, correctly respecting the packet's UNVERIFIABLE ruling. Most impressively, the Guerra sign convention at line 105 reproduces the packet's REFUTED-item correction exactly, including the explicit statement of Guerra's convention. The factual failures below are omissions and attribution gaps, not falsehoods.

The Fortuin-Kasteleyn random-cluster representation, which is the entire technical payload of the percolation section (lines 51-55), is presented with no attribution to anyone. The chapter also introduces 'the q-state Potts model' as a term with no citation. This is the one place in the chapter where a substantive result is stated with no source at all, and it happens to be the section's load-bearing argument. The packet contains no entry for it, which means the chapter reached outside its evidence base precisely where it needed a citation most.

'the de Almeida-Thouless line' (line 101) names two people and a named result with no citation anywhere in the chapter or its reference list. The phrase occurs in the packet only inside the body text of the Fisher-Huse and Parisi entries; there is no verifiedClaim for de Almeida and Thouless's own 1978 paper. The chapter leans on the AT line for a full sentence of argument ('In mean-field theory the replica-symmetric solution is unstable not only below the zero-field freezing temperature but along a line in the temperature-field plane') and sources none of it.

The universal stiffness jump at line 33 ('at the transition the dimensionless stiffness K/k_B T equals 2/pi whatever the film is made of, and above the transition the stiffness vanishes') is stated as the chapter's one strong universal prediction and attributed to nobody. This is the Nelson-Kosterlitz result, and it is the single most experimentally consequential statement in the BKT section.

Line 65's 'an itinerant magnet in three dimensions with z = 2 has d_eff = 5' is unsupported and, as an example, poorly chosen. z = 2 is the itinerant antiferromagnetic case; z = 3 is the clean itinerant ferromagnet, which is Hertz's own headline case and the case the chapter's own Chubukov-Pepin-Rech paragraph (line 77) is about. The chapter never tells the reader which is which, so the one worked number in the section floats free of any physical system.

Line 15 asserts Kosterlitz and Thouless 'defined topological order for two-dimensional systems' without giving the year 1973 anywhere in the body. The date appears only in the reference list. For a chapter whose spine is chronology (1966, 1970/71, 1974, 1975, 1979, 1983), silently dropping the date of its own hinge paper is careless.
whatWouldMakeItAAA: Four things, in order of severity. First, fix the spine or change it. Either the chapter's cases genuinely share a failure mode and the chapter must say what it actually is, or they do not and the chapter should say so openly, which is the more interesting claim: percolation loses the free energy but keeps the order parameter, quantum criticality keeps both but loses experimental access to the critical point, BKT keeps the free energy but has no local order parameter, and the spin glass loses the very type of the order parameter. That is a genuine taxonomy of four distinct ways the Landau-Wilson apparatus can break, and it is a better chapter than the false one currently asserted at line 9. Second, the book has to show up. This is chapter 3 of a book about AI and phase transitions, and the packet's own outline says these exceptions are the ground where machine learning has been most useful because human order-parameter intuition runs out. That argument should be in the chapter, load-bearing, not deferred to Part Six with one clause. The closing move at line 115 is the right instinct and it is the only place the book's real subject nearly surfaces; it should be the chapter's engine, not its exit line. Third, pay off the opening. State the negative entropy, show why replica symmetry produces it, and connect it to de Almeida and Thouless, who are the people who actually established which part of the ansatz failed and whom the chapter currently strands in an unrelated paragraph seventy lines later. The BKT section proves the author can carry a real derivation in clean prose; the spin-glass section, which is the chapter's climax, must be given the same treatment, including at minimum the nested block construction that produces q(x) from a finite-step matrix. Fourth, kill the metadata voice. Every full legal name goes to surname on second mention and most on first. Disambiguate the two Fishers. Attribute Fortuin and Kasteleyn, Nelson and Kosterlitz, and de Almeida and Thouless, or cut the results that depend on them. Replace the enumerative topic sentences at lines 47 and 59 with transitions that carry an argument. Rewrite every passage that currently paraphrases the research packet, starting with Millis at line 75, from the physics rather than from the dossier, since the dossier itself warns that its Millis description was never read off the paper.
